overview: 1...b5 is a hypermodern reply that aims ...Bb7 against the e4/g2 squares and ...a6 or ...e6. White usually answers e4 or Nf3 and has the easier centre, but Black's flank play is annoying rather than bad. Evidence is thin.

white_ideas.idea: Take the centre with e4 and Nf3
Hit the b5 pawn with Bxb5 or a4
Play Nf3 and g3 for a solid Bird set-up

black_ideas.idea: Develop ...Bb7 to hit g2 and e4
Use ...a6 to hold the b5 pawn

typical_structures.structure: Black has queenside space but no central pawns

character.notes: Flank play with few forcing lines.

gambit.notes: At the root material is level and nothing is attacked yet.

sublines_that_differ.name: Immediate e4
sublines_that_differ.how: White grabs the pawn and Black regains with ...Bxe4.

character.reason: Flank play with the pieces slowly developing and no forcing lines.

gambit.reason: At the root material is level and nothing is attacked yet.

soundness.reason: Black's ...b5 is odd but not refuted.

structure.reason: The centre is undecided at move one.

approach.reason: Strong players hardly ever answer 1.f4 with ...b5.

level.reason: It has simple ideas but is not a standard repertoire choice.

plans.reason: The ...Bb7 fianchetto is Black's main idea.
